haiku-low.q1: The scheduler starts it at 02:00 UTC nightly, or on retry or manual rerun. It extracts replica orders with updated_at after hwm minus 2 hours, up to the replay-timestamp cutoff.
haiku-low.q2: A bulk import's transaction can stay open up to 90 minutes, so its rows can become visible on the replica up to 90 minutes after their updated_at.
haiku-low.q3: The next runs re-read it through the 2-hour lookback if visible in time. The merge then replaces the stored row, since the edit's updated_at is newer.
haiku-low.q4: Nothing is removed. The soft delete is a write that bumps updated_at, so the merge sets is_deleted to true on the row, which stays in orders_current.
haiku-low.q5: The attempt rolls back, staging is dropped, and its run log row is marked failed. The lock is released if the host is alive. A retry starts 15 minutes later from the same hwm; the third failure pages on-call.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards show the last committed night, with nothing half-loaded. The watchdog at 06:00 UTC posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday reconciliation compares each of the last 30 creation days against the replica and reloads any mismatched day from the replica, with updated_at up to H.
haiku-low.q8: Step 7 keeps only the highest updated_at per order_id, with a row hash tie-break. The merge then updates a row only when the incoming updated_at is strictly newer.
haiku-low.q9: It is stored in etl_watermark as hwm. At commit (step 9), in the same warehouse transaction as the merge, it is set to the cutoff read at step 3.
haiku-low.q10: The merge, the hwm update and the run log update commit in one warehouse transaction. Dashboards read only committed orders_current, so they see a whole night or none.
haiku-low.q11: Staging is per run id and is dropped in the failure path, so the retry never uses it. The retry extracts the same window again from the same hwm.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads that day's rows with updated_at up to H from the replica, applies them by the same never-deleting merge under the lock, and does not move the nightly hwm.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts it at 02:00 UTC (retries and manual reruns use the same entry point). It extracts replica `orders` rows with updated_at after hwm minus 2 hours, up to the cutoff (the replica's pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp()).
sonnet.q2: updated_at is set when the row is written, but a bulk import's transaction can stay open up to 90 minutes, and the rows become visible only at commit. So they appear on the replica up to 90 minutes after their updated_at.
sonnet.q3: The edit bumps updated_at, so a later nightly window picks it up. The merge updates the stored row because the incoming updated_at is strictly newer.
sonnet.q4: A soft delete is a write that sets deleted_at and bumps updated_at. The next load merges it like any update: the row stays in orders_current with is_deleted set true. Rows are never removed.
sonnet.q5: The scheduler stops the attempt: marks the run log row failed, rolls back any open transaction, drops staging, and releases the lock. The scheduler retries 15 minutes later from the same hwm. After the third failed attempt for the night, on-call is paged with the run id and error. The hwm does not move.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards show the previous committed night, with nothing half-loaded. The watchdog at 06:00 posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts. (Failed attempts page on-call after the third failure.)
sonnet.q7: The Sunday weekly reconciliation. It compares count and checksum per creation day over the last 30 days. On a mismatch it reloads that day from the replica with the same merge.
sonnet.q8: The merge updates a matched row only when the incoming updated_at is strictly newer. Unchanged or older rows are left alone, so re-runs are no-ops. Step 7 also keeps only the newest row per order_id within the extract, with a row hash as the tie-break.
sonnet.q9: In the warehouse table etl_watermark (one row with hwm, last_committed_run_id, committed_at). It is set to the cutoff, in step 9, inside the same warehouse transaction as the merge, at commit.
sonnet.q10: The merge, the hwm update and the run log update commit in one warehouse transaction. orders_current changes only at that commit, and the dashboard views read committed data only, so they see all of a night or none of it.
sonnet.q11: Staging is dropped when the failed attempt ends, and the retry uses its own run id, so it has its own staging table. The retry starts from the same hwm, so it extracts the same window: updated_at after hwm minus 2 hours, up to a new cutoff read at its step 3.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads that creation day's rows from the replica with updated_at <= H (H is the hwm the Sunday load committed). It takes the pipeline lock, applies them with the same merge (an upsert that never deletes), and releases the lock at that day's commit. It does not move the hwm.
